card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent finds the row hash idea and gets part of the speedup, but not the tag-comparison SIMD or the full gain at the highest levels. A weaker model makes micro-tweaks only.
card.cheat: Hardcoding a lower level or weakening the search is caught by the ratio floor. Caching or precomputing is blocked by hidden inputs and fresh processes. The v1.5.0 source is not shipped.
card.grading: Hard gate: every output round-trips through the baseline decoder, and the decoder is byte-exact on a hidden corpus. A compression-ratio floor is set at 1% loss against the baseline. Wall-clock medians are taken on a hidden corpus (text, binaries, logs, over 128 KB) at levels 5-12 and in decode. Reward is 2^u-1 against our measured speedup.
card.reference: The upstream v1.5.0 tree, measured at 1.25x to 2.4x on compression and a few percent on decode.
card.source: https://github.com/facebook/zstd v1.4.9 -> v1.5.0, BSD-3-Clause (dual with GPLv2)
card.task: /app ships a history-less zstd v1.4.9 snapshot with its CLI and library build. The agent makes compression levels 5-12 and decompression faster. The levers are a row-based match finder with tag matching, a restructured decode loop and reduced stack use, while keeping the format valid.
card.title: Zstd 1.4.9 to 1.5.0 row match finder and decode loop speedup

source_notes: Levers: (1) new row-based match finder for greedy/lazy/lazy2 (2) decompression loop refactor (PRs #2614 #2630) (3) reduced stack use in entropy stage (PRs #2522 #2524). INFERRED: compressed bytes likely change with the new match finder, so gate on round-trip and ratio rather than byte-identical compressed output (decompression side is byte-identical). Only SSE2 CPUs get full gain. q:"The biggest gains are achieved on files typically larger than 128KB." Compression-only lever count is small, decode side adds second lever family. Licence stated on repo not on release page.
source_version: zstd v1.4.9 (INFERRED: prior release; page gives no explicit baseline tag) -> zstd v1.5.0

facts.claim: Zstandard v1.5.0 release exists on facebook/zstd (tag v1.5.0, released 14 May)
v1.5.0 release notes make a new match finder the default for greedy, lazy and lazy2 strategies
v1.5.0 changelog lists decompression loop refactor and reduced stack usage in the entropy stage
Full gain only on SSE2-capable CPUs; biggest gains on files typically larger than 128KB; legacy finder used below 16KB
Release page itself names the feature 'row-based' or describes row hash / tag matching
Release-page speedup table (about +25% at level 5 to +110-140% at level 12, i9-9900K)
LICENSE file at v1.5.0 is BSD (three-clause conditions, no PATENTS grant)
PR #2614 (decoder long-sequence prefetch) merged 5 May 2021 into dev; decode-side, not match finder
PR #2630 (gcc-9/10 decoding alignment) merged 10 May 2021; decode-side
PR #2522 (reduce stack usage of ZSTD_buildCTable, entropy stage) merged 5 Mar 2021
PR #2524 is a stack-reduction change merged into v1.5.0
Later release v1.5.5 further sped up the row match finder and fixed a corruption bug at levels 16+ (so upstream direction has moved past v1.5.0)

full_card.band: 8 h. Frontier likely finds row finder and part of speedup; full gain at high levels and tag SIMD are the hard buckets; weaker model micro-tweaks. Unverified by dated public evidence.
full_card.build_cost: 3 days: hidden corpus, fresh-process timing harness, ratio/round-trip gate, building reference, enabling ctest (smoke run_rcs=8 with zero tests means tests not registered; need ZSTD_BUILD_TESTS config).
full_card.deliverable: Faster compression at levels 5-12 (row-based match finder with tag matching, SSE2 path) and faster decompression (decode loop restructure, lower stack use), output still valid zstd decodable by baseline decoder.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden inputs and fresh processes block precompute/caching; ratio floor blocks weakened search; v1.5.0 source not shipped. Open gap: system libzstd in base image (not verified; spike must check) could be linked or copied as a faster oracle.
full_card.grading_surface: Hard gate: round-trip through baseline decoder on every output; byte-exact decode on hidden corpus (text, binaries, logs >128KB); ratio floor 1% loss; wall-clock medians levels 5-12 and decode; reward 2^u-1.
full_card.local_fit: C, cmake, 8 cores, 16 GB, CPU-only, offline; build 13 s. Timing under gVisor noisy; SSE2 lever x86-only.
full_card.lookup: partial: row-finder outline and tag design are public and partly recallable; no code in image beyond v1.4.9; later v1.5.5 exists (must stay on snapshot).
full_card.provenance: facebook/zstd, BSD LICENSE + GPLv2 COPYING at v1.5.0; upstream v1.5.0 tag public (14 May 2021 per release page). Base snapshot v1.4.9 history-less.
full_card.reference: Upstream v1.5.0 tree; upstream release notes show gains, measured on other hardware (i9-9900K), must be re-measured in sandbox.
full_card.ships: Zstd v1.4.9 C source snapshot (no git history, no v1.5.x tree) with cmake CLI and library build; ~40 MB repo, 269 test files.
full_card.similarity: Max l0 neighbour 0.209 (zstd-decoder SWE-Marathon), zstd ProgramBench 0.156. Codec subject is on CROWDED list, but deliverable is speed optimization with timing gates, not a clone; not K1.

Band.why: Seed band is plausible, but there is no dated public evidence of agent results on this kind of task, so capped at 3.

Build.why: About 3 days: corpus, harness, determinism, tests registration, reference build.

Fit.why: Offline C/cmake fits the sandbox. Timing noise under gVisor and the SSE2 dependency are the risks.

Hor.why: Row finder, tag SIMD, decode loop and stack work across several modules is a sustained 8 h effort.

Lic.why: BSD LICENSE confirmed; shipping permitted. The GPLv2 dual claim is not confirmed, but that does not block shipping.

Multi.why: Separate buckets per level (5-12) and decode, plus several independent levers.

Nov.why: Max neighbour 0.209; zstd is on the CROWDED list but this is an optimization deliverable, not a clone.

Real.why: facebook/zstd is a real, 28k-star project with tagged v1.4.9 and v1.5.0 releases.

Ref.why: Upstream v1.5.0 is a strong reference, but its speedup was measured on other hardware and must be re-measured here.

Seal.why: Upstream is public and famous, but a history-less v1.4.9 snapshot keeps the reference out of reach. Drops to 2 if a system libzstd >=1.5 is in the image.

Surf.why: Executable oracle (round-trip plus byte-exact decode) over a hidden corpus at many levels; timing medians add buckets.

spike_plan.kill_if: System libzstd >=1.5 cannot be removed or excluded from grading (K11); reference speedup below 1.1x or above 3x on our hardware (K8/K9 recalibration); timings not reproducible within 10% (K4); decode gain indistinguishable from noise (drop decode bucket, not a full kill).
spike_plan.pass_if: Reference speedup 1.25x-2.4x at levels 5-12 on our hardware; decode gain measurable; round-trip byte-exact; ratio loss <=1%; timing variance <=5% over repeats; no system libzstd >=1.5 reachable from the snapshot build.
steps: In a throwaway networked Debian container matching the base image, run dpkg -l | grep -i zstd and ldconfig -p | grep zstd; record any libzstd1 version and whether zstd CLI exists. If libzstd >=1.5 is present, plan to remove it or verify the grader ignores it before continuing.
Clone facebook/zstd, check out the v1.4.9 base commit and the v1.5.0 tag. Build both with cmake (-DZSTD_BUILD_TESTS=ON so ctest registers tests); confirm base tests pass.
Build a small corpus of 6-8 files over 128KB (text, ELF binaries, logs, mixed) and run zstd -b5 -e12 style timing per level for base and v1.5.0, 3 repetitions each, record medians.
Check the compression speedup at levels 5-12 falls in roughly 1.25x-2.4x on this hardware, and that decode gain is measurable above noise (a few percent).
Round-trip: compress each file with v1.5.0 at levels 5-12, decode with the v1.4.9 decoder, confirm byte-exact output and ratio loss <=1% vs v1.4.9.
Repeat timings on a second run to check medians vary by less than about 5%.

v1.summary: The upstream v1.5.0 release, the BSD LICENSE, and the decode and stack PRs (#2614, #2630, #2522) are confirmed, so the seed's levers are real, public and sealable as a v1.4.9 snapshot. Not killed, but the spike must confirm the reference speedup on our hardware and rule out a system libzstd in the image, and the smoke run shows zero registered tests, so the build cost is about 3 days.

v2.note: Release-note paper trail confirmed, but the speedup table was not found and must be re-measured in gVisor. Most of the gain is one lever, the row match finder, and frontier models know zstd_lazy.c in detail (K8 watch). The decode bucket is only a few percent and may be lost in noise. Debian images usually carry libzstd1 1.5.x, which could be dlopen'd as a faster engine, so the grader must check linkage. zstd is on the CROWDED list as a codec, although here the deliverable is a speedup.
